title: Meta Muse Memory.md, Privacy & How to Reset Safely
description: What Meta Muse stores in Memory.md, how to view or delete saved personal facts, and how to reset Memory.md without wiping Soul.md.
h1: Meta Muse Memory.md, privacy, and how to reset safely.
dek: Memory.md stores facts about your work and preferences across chats. Here is how to audit it, prune stale entries, or clear it without losing your Soul.md tuning.
lede: Meta Muse stores personal facts and project context in Memory.md under Assistant Identity. Over weeks of use, Memory.md can collect one-off notes or finished project details that start bleeding into unrelated chats. Here is how to audit and reset Memory.md in two minutes without touching your Soul.md personality rules.
answer: Open Settings → Personalization → Assistant Identity (or tap the Assistant icon) and select Memory.md to view, edit, or delete saved facts about you. To clear old context without losing your communication style, reset only Memory.md and leave Soul.md and Identity.md untouched.

sections.html:
In Meta Muse, Memory.md is the notebook where Muse records ongoing facts about you. Unlike Soul.md (how Muse talks) and Identity.md (Muse’s name and avatar), Memory.md updates over time as you chat:

Belongs in Memory.mdMove to Soul.md insteadDelete from both
Your role, primary programming languages, or recurring deliverables.Rules like "lead with the answer" or "use plain prose instead of bullet lists."One-time trip dates, finished sprint tasks, or old debugging logs.
Standing domain context (target audience or style guide name).How strongly you want Muse to push back on weak arguments.Sensitive credentials, client secrets, or private identifiers.
Tools and environment defaults you use every week.Formatting defaults for code blocks, tables, and summaries.Contradictory notes added automatically from a single brainstorm chat.

sections.h2: Why stale Memory.md entries make Muse feel repetitive.
sections.html: When a temporary project note gets saved into Memory.md, Muse loads that note into future sessions and can force awkward connections to finished work. Whenever Muse keeps referencing an old topic, inspect Memory.md first—or paste its contents into our local AI Memory Reviewer to uncheck duplicates and stale entries.

sections.h2: How to audit or reset Memory.md without wiping Soul.md.
sections.html:
You can clean up Memory.md in settings or directly from Main Chat:

  1. Open Settings → Personalization → Assistant Identity → Memory.md (or tap the Assistant icon → Memory).
  2. Delete outdated bullets, or replace the file with a short list of durable facts.

If you manage it in Main Chat, name Memory.md explicitly so Muse leaves Soul.md untouched:

Show me the current contents of Memory.md grouped into: (1) durable work context, (2) personal preferences, and (3) one-off task notes. Do not edit Soul.md or Identity.md.

To clear stale notes while keeping your role and tools:

Clear all project-specific and temporary entries from Memory.md, keeping only my role and primary tools. Leave Soul.md and Identity.md completely unchanged, and show me the updated Memory.md before saving.

sections.h2: A clean Memory.md structure that stays easy to prune.
sections.html:
Split Memory.md into two short headings so monthly cleanups take 30 seconds:

# Memory ## Durable context - Role: Product engineer working on web applications in TypeScript and Python. - Audience: Technical teammates; skip beginner explanations of standard library APIs. ## Active projects (review monthly) - Current focus: Static site build tooling and search analytics.

Then keep your communication rules in Soul.md (and tell Muse not to over-use saved memories):

## How to work with me - Answer the question first, then give supporting detail only when needed. - Use saved facts from Memory.md only when they are directly relevant to the current task. - Do not force connections to my past projects in unrelated conversations. - Ask before saving temporary task constraints to Memory.md.

faq.q: How do I see what Meta Muse remembers about me?
faq.a: Open Settings, then Personalization, then Assistant Identity, and select Memory.md, or ask Muse in chat to print the current contents of Memory.md.

faq.q: Does clearing Memory.md delete my Soul.md personality tuning?
faq.a: No, as long as you edit or clear only Memory.md. Soul.md and Identity.md are separate files under Assistant Identity.

faq.q: How do I stop Meta Muse from bringing up old topics in every chat?
faq.a: Delete finished projects and one-off notes from Memory.md, and add a line in Soul.md instructing Muse to use saved memory only when directly relevant to the current prompt.

faq.q: Should I put formatting rules in Memory.md or Soul.md?
faq.a: Put formatting, tone, and length rules in Soul.md. Keep Memory.md strictly for factual context about your work, tools, and ongoing projects.
